# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

135	Correct the affected inference node or default, publish if the definition changed, and restart
136	the API if process defaults changed before starting a new run. This pinned argument refusal has no Resume: repeating its saved request would send
137	the same rejected choice. Keep the original run and its delivery provenance; do not infer
138	that no effects occurred from the top-level failure alone. GraphGoblin does not fall back to
139	another model, repeatedly retry the refusal, or disable a shipped model for every account.
140	
141	An LLM decision deliberately omits provider text. A refused Codex route request instead records
142	`EVALUATION_PROVIDER_FAILED`, `details.code: DECIDER_HTTP_ERROR`, and “Decision provider request
143	failed,” with no Resume. That safe category cannot establish an account restriction. Check the
144	decision's selected model against the login and endpoint, choose a supported combination,
145	correct and publish the decision, and start a new run. Keep the original failure; do not infer
146	an account-specific explanation from that generic category.
147	
148	## Find the symptom
149	
150	For `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, the previous script attempt may already have produced its effect before its result was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed. Inspect the external system, then choose **Recover script**: **Resume** runs it again in the same run; **Replay** runs it in a new run from the failed node; **Cancel** leaves the run failed. Either retry may repeat the effect. `SCRIPT_START_FAILED` instead means the runner proved the command did not start. Restore an external prerequisite, such as a missing executable, then explicitly Resume. To change the command, arguments or working-directory configuration, start a fresh run from the corrected definition: use a published version for the UI's **New run**, or test the saved draft [through the API](03-run-and-observe.md#start-through-the-api) with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`. Neither Resume nor Replay applies the change because both keep the pinned version. See [Windows batch commands](#windows-batch-commands). Nonzero completed exits retain `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`. The failure's `script` fields identify the visit, dispatch, state and known exit code.
151	
152	After upgrading, an unfinished script visit from an earlier build may have no dispatch marker even though it already produced an effect. Recovery classifies it as `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` with a visit ID and no dispatch ID; it does not run the command. The same failure and recovery choices remain available if writing a dispatched script's progress or completion failed. Repair the storage fault, inspect any external effect, then choose Resume or Replay knowingly, or leave the run failed with Cancel. No store reset or migration is required.
153

201	### Windows batch commands
202	
203	Script commands run without an implicit shell. On Windows, naming a `.cmd` or `.bat` file as
204	the command fails with `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`: the process runner proved that it did not start.
205	This is distinct from `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, which needs explicit recovery consent because
206	an earlier attempt may have produced effects. A proven start refusal permits ordinary Resume,
207	but Resume and Replay both use the failed run's pinned command, arguments and working-directory
208	configuration.
209	
210	To run a batch file, explicitly choose `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` (use your Windows
211	installation's actual path), set its arguments to `/d`, `/c` and the intended batch command,
212	and choose the working directory deliberately. `/d` disables the command processor's AutoRun
213	commands. The command string after `/c` is interpreted by that shell; keep it authored and
214	quote paths and arguments for `cmd.exe`, rather than inserting untrusted text. For example,
215	with a working directory containing `build.cmd`, the arguments are `["/d", "/c", "build.cmd"]`.
216	Start a fresh run from the corrected definition. The UI's **New run** uses a published version,
217	so publish the correction before starting it there. To test an unpublished saved draft, use
218	`POST /loops/{id}/runs` with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`; the run
219	freezes a new snapshot without publication. Publishing can arm the new version's cron and
220	webhook triggers and disable the earlier version's registrations; see
221	[trigger arming](../08-triggers-and-integrations.md#arming-decided-shipped-in-m6).
222	Neither Resume nor Replay applies a definition change; both retain the old batch-file command.
223	If only an external prerequisite changed, such as
224	restoring a missing executable, Resume can use the existing pinned definition.

231	identity. Find heartbeat failures by the same run failure code in the inspector.

Correct the affected inference node or default, publish if the definition changed, and restart
the API if process defaults changed before starting a new run. This pinned argument refusal has no Resume: repeating its saved request would send
the same rejected choice. Keep the original run and its delivery provenance; do not infer
that no effects occurred from the top-level failure alone. GraphGoblin does not fall back to
another model, repeatedly retry the refusal, or disable a shipped model for every account.

An LLM decision deliberately omits provider text. A refused Codex route request instead records
`EVALUATION_PROVIDER_FAILED`, `details.code: DECIDER_HTTP_ERROR`, and “Decision provider request
failed,” with no Resume. That safe category cannot establish an account restriction. Check the
decision's selected model against the login and endpoint, choose a supported combination,
correct and publish the decision, and start a new run. Keep the original failure; do not infer
an account-specific explanation from that generic category.

## Find the symptom

For `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, the previous script attempt may already have produced its effect before its result was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed. Inspect the external system, then choose **Recover script**: **Resume** runs it again in the same run; **Replay** runs it in a new run from the failed node; **Cancel** leaves the run failed. Either retry may repeat the effect. `SCRIPT_START_FAILED` instead means the runner proved the command did not start. Restore an external prerequisite, such as a missing executable, then explicitly Resume. To change the command, arguments or working-directory configuration, start a fresh run from the corrected definition: use a published version for the UI's **New run**, or test the saved draft [through the API](03-run-and-observe.md#start-through-the-api) with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`. Neither Resume nor Replay applies the change because both keep the pinned version. See [Windows batch commands](#windows-batch-commands). Nonzero completed exits retain `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`. The failure's `script` fields identify the visit, dispatch, state and known exit code.

After upgrading, an unfinished script visit from an earlier build may have no dispatch marker even though it already produced an effect. Recovery classifies it as `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` with a visit ID and no dispatch ID; it does not run the command. The same failure and recovery choices remain available if writing a dispatched script's progress or completion failed. Repair the storage fault, inspect any external effect, then choose Resume or Replay knowingly, or leave the run failed with Cancel. No store reset or migration is required.

### Windows batch commands

Script commands run without an implicit shell. On Windows, naming a `.cmd` or `.bat` file as
the command fails with `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`: the process runner proved that it did not start.
This is distinct from `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, which needs explicit recovery consent because
an earlier attempt may have produced effects. A proven start refusal permits ordinary Resume,
but Resume and Replay both use the failed run's pinned command, arguments and working-directory
configuration.

To run a batch file, explicitly choose `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` (use your Windows
installation's actual path), set its arguments to `/d`, `/c` and the intended batch command,
and choose the working directory deliberately. `/d` disables the command processor's AutoRun
commands. The command string after `/c` is interpreted by that shell; keep it authored and
quote paths and arguments for `cmd.exe`, rather than inserting untrusted text. For example,
with a working directory containing `build.cmd`, the arguments are `["/d", "/c", "build.cmd"]`.
Start a fresh run from the corrected definition. The UI's **New run** uses a published version,
so publish the correction before starting it there. To test an unpublished saved draft, use
`POST /loops/{id}/runs` with the editable draft's `versionId` and `allowDraft: true`; the run
freezes a new snapshot without publication. Publishing can arm the new version's cron and
webhook triggers and disable the earlier version's registrations; see
[trigger arming](../08-triggers-and-integrations.md#arming-decided-shipped-in-m6).
Neither Resume nor Replay applies a definition change; both retain the old batch-file command.
If only an external prerequisite changed, such as
restoring a missing executable, Resume can use the existing pinned definition.

## HTTP probe exceeds 64 KiB

HTTP polls and heartbeat probes fail above 65,536 decompressed response bytes with
`HTTP_PROBE_BODY_OVERFLOW`; partial JSON is never presented as success. Find polls
in API log warnings named `poll trigger failed` with that code and the loop/trigger
identity. Find heartbeat failures by the same run failure code in the inspector.

Single-result HTTP probes formerly parsed the full JSON while slicing the body

# 08 - Triggers and integrations

Stored trigger configs use `type`: `manual`, `cron`, `webhook`, `event`, or `poll`.
Webhooks use one strict `type: 'webhook'` object with nested authentication, body and event-type configuration. Config parsers reject
`subtype`; stores and exports that still use it are in an older format and are refused,
not converted ([ADR-0042](decisions/ADR-0042-explicit-resets-replace-conversion.md)).
The invocation envelope continues to record the source as `trigger.kind`.

## Trigger envelope (Decided)

Every trigger source produces the same envelope, embedded in the invocation and therefore in the thread.

```ts
type TriggerEnvelope = {
  nodeId: string;
  kind: 'manual' | 'cron' | 'webhook' | 'event' | 'poll';
  payload: unknown;
  receivedAt: string;
  dedupeKey?: string;
};
```

Nothing in the core knows about GitHub, CI systems, or error trackers. Provider-specific behavior is expressed through presets that fill in signature settings and dedupe keys for a generic webhook and add editable downstream checks.

## Manual (Decided)

Three surfaces, one path: the UI button, `POST /loops/{id}/runs`, and the `start_run` MCP tool all create an invocation with the trigger node's input validated against its `inputSchema`. The `exposeTo` setting on the node controls which surfaces show it.

## Arming (Decided, shipped in M6)

The `TriggerService` in `apps/api/src/triggers/` owns everything between an external signal and `RunManager.startRun`.

- `POST /loops/{id}/publish` arms the new version: one `schedules` row per cron trigger node and one `webhook_endpoints` row per webhook trigger node. Rows of earlier versions of the loop are disabled, not deleted, so `GET /loops/{id}/triggers` shows the history. Runs in flight are unaffected (ADR-0008).
- Publishing is refused with 422 `LOOP_INVALID` (issue code `CRON_INVALID`) when a cron expression or timezone does not parse.
- Boot re-arms every loop's current version. Arming is idempotent per version: existing rows keep their next fire time, so a restart still sees what it missed, and a restored database without trigger rows gets them back.
- Deleting a loop disables its rows.
- `GET /loops/{id}/triggers` lists schedules, webhook endpoints (as `path: /hooks/<token>`, never the secret), and armed poll triggers.

## Cron (Decided, shipped in M6)

- The trigger editor offers six schedule presets, a searchable IANA timezone picker (default UTC), a summary, and the next five slots in both the trigger and viewer zones. Raw cron lives under the schedule's Advanced disclosure; custom expressions are preserved. The read-only `POST /triggers/cron/preview` calls `CronScheduler.nextFire` and requires `loops:read`; an invalid expression or zone returns 400 `CRON_INVALID` before publishing (see 07 and guide 04).
- croner (MIT) computes slots in the trigger's `timezone`, including daylight-saving changes. The next fire time is persisted in `schedules.next_fire_at`.
- `CronScheduler` in `packages/infrastructure/src/scheduler` polls for due schedules every `GG_TIMER_POLL_MS` (default 1 s). A schedule is advanced in the store before its listeners run, so a crash mid-fire loses at most that fire and never repeats it.
- At boot, before polling starts, each enabled schedule whose next fire time is already past applies its `missedFirePolicy`: `skip` moves to the next future slot without firing; `run-once` fires one catch-up run for the latest missed slot; `run-each` retains the latest missed slots, up to `RUN_EACH_CAP` (100) per schedule, and fires them oldest first. Past the cap the older slots are dropped with a warning naming the number dropped and the first retained slot; a minutely schedule down for a day would otherwise start 1,440 runs at once.
- A firing starts a run with `source: 'cron'`, `triggerKind: 'cron'`, payload `{ scheduledFor, catchUp }`, and dedupe key `cron:<scheduleId>:<scheduledFor>`.
- Overlapping fires start parallel runs, per the concurrency decision.

The `run-each` catch-up cap does not change `run-once` semantics. Even after an
outage longer than 100 slots, `run-once` uses the latest missed slot at or before
the recovery clock.

## General webhook configuration (#168 T4)

A Webhook accepts an ordinary POST at `/hooks/<token>`. Tokens remain stable across versions for the same trigger node. The pinned definition owns `body`, `eventType`, `dedupeKey`. The endpoint row owns its safe authentication recipe; intake requires exact agreement with that pinned definition and owner/loop/version provenance before resolving a secret.

```ts
{
  type: 'webhook',
  authentication: { type: 'none' }, // default
  body: { type: 'json' },          // default
  eventType: { source: 'constant', value: 'webhook' }, // default
  dedupeKey?: Expression,
}
```

All objects are strict; flat `signature` and `replayWindowSeconds` fields are rejected. None establishes no sender identity. The same endpoint lookup, 60/minute default limiter, 1 MiB raw bound (including chunked bodies), decoding, extraction and atomic admission apply to every recipe.

| Authentication                                                                     | Fields and signing message                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{type:'none'}`                                                                    | No signing fields or secret lookup; no authenticated sender identity.                                                                  |

file.content:
Every run, draft runs included, executes one immutable definition record for its whole life.
`RunRecord.versionId` names it and `RunRecord.pinned` describes it:
`{ source: 'published' | 'draft', version, name, label, defaults: { owner, process }, classifiers }`,
where `classifiers` maps each classifier id the definition uses to the catalog binding it calls
(`provider`, `providerModel`, `endpoint`, `primitives`, `secretRef?`; never the secret value).
The start responses (`POST /loops/{id}/runs`, `POST /runs/{id}/replay`, MCP `start_run`) return it,
and the first event of every run, `run.queued`, carries the same `versionId` and `pinned`, so the
SSE stream identifies the definition before anything runs. A draft start
(`{ versionId: <draft id>, allowDraft: true }`) answers with a new `versionId`: the draft snapshot
taken at start, readable at `GET /loops/{id}/versions/{versionId}` (status `snapshot`) and never
listed in the version history. Starting a snapshot directly answers 409 `VERSION_NOT_PUBLISHED`.
`label` and `name` are those of the pinned definition, so renaming or editing the loop later does
not change them. MCP compact runs (`list_runs`, control tools) include `definition`, the label.

100	## Inference prompt delivery
101	
102	Inspect `failure.inference.submission` and the visit's `harness.turn` / `harness.submission`
103	events. A session ID or init announcement alone proves no prompt acceptance.
104	
105	For non-pinned generic failures, Codex permits Resume even when the adapter reports
106	`retriable: false` for an exit or lost stream. Claude requires the adapter's `retriable`
107	evidence. Both still need a usable session for uncertain recovery; pinned unsupported-policy,
108	configuration and argument refusals remain non-resumable.
109	
110	| Case                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
111	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
112	| Definitely not submitted (`definitely-not-submitted`)                                                                                                                                                        | Fix the external cause and Resume when eligible: the exact saved authored/repair task uses its original session selection. Unsupported policy, invalid configuration and rejected arguments need a corrected definition and a new run; the failed run's definition is pinned.                                                                                                                                                                         |
113	| Delivery uncertain (`HARNESS_DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN`, or a specific timeout/quota/storage cause with `delivery-uncertain`)                                                                                       | When eligible, Resume continues a usable recorded session. An inherited previous/named ID without authored-task acceptance is insufficient. When non-resumable, inspect possible effects and use **Replay from the node** for a deliberate attempt. Stop an unconfirmed native process first.                                                                                                                                                         |
114	| The provider refused the request (`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with `details.adapterCode: HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`; the message starts `The provider refused the request (HTTP 400, …)` and quotes the provider) | The provider refused a value the run's pinned definition sends, such as an effort or model it does not accept for this model or account. The failure keeps this cause even when the provenance says `delivery-uncertain` (Codex had already taken the prompt into its conversation). Resume is never offered, because the same request would be refused again. Correct the node, decision or default the message names, publish, and start a new run. |
115	| Session missing (`HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING`)                                                                                                                                                                  | Preserve and inspect the failed run. Resume is refused. Use **Replay from the node** for a deliberate attempt; named-session lookup can still select the same missing conversation. To change that policy, correct the definition and start a new run. For eligible failures use the explicit Start fresh session control described below (#265).                                                                                                     |
116	
117	## Codex model unavailable for this account or endpoint
118	
119	For a Codex inference turn, check the failed run's message, not just its top-level code. A structured provider refusal
120	(`HTTP 400`, `invalid_request_error`) appears as `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with
121	`details.adapterCode: HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`, followed by the provider's explanation.
122	When that explanation says the selected model is unavailable for the account or endpoint,
123	it identifies the cause of that request. A generic failure, malformed output, or an
124	unknown/transient error does not by itself establish an account restriction.
125	
126	An enabled catalogue row and a successful **Retry preflight** do not test model access.
127	Preflight checks installation, CLI capabilities and login without sending a model turn.
128	Shipped model definitions and the bundled CLI's static plan information do not measure current
129	access; GraphGoblin's catalogue has no account-plan field. The `gpt-5.5` ChatGPT-account refusal reported in
130	[October 2026](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/427) is historical evidence,
131	not a current availability claim for your account. An API-key login is not a guaranteed remedy.
132	
133	Choose a model the provider supports for the login and endpoint used by the API process, or
134	deliberately change that user's Codex login/provider configuration to a supported choice.
135	Correct the affected inference node or default, publish if the definition changed, and restart

## Inference prompt delivery

Inspect `failure.inference.submission` and the visit's `harness.turn` / `harness.submission`
events. A session ID or init announcement alone proves no prompt acceptance.

For non-pinned generic failures, Codex permits Resume even when the adapter reports
`retriable: false` for an exit or lost stream. Claude requires the adapter's `retriable`
evidence. Both still need a usable session for uncertain recovery; pinned unsupported-policy,
configuration and argument refusals remain non-resumable.

| Case                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Definitely not submitted (`definitely-not-submitted`)                                                                                                                                                        | Fix the external cause and Resume when eligible: the exact saved authored/repair task uses its original session selection. Unsupported policy, invalid configuration and rejected arguments need a corrected definition and a new run; the failed run's definition is pinned.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Delivery uncertain (`HARNESS_DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN`, or a specific timeout/quota/storage cause with `delivery-uncertain`)                                                                                       | When eligible, Resume continues a usable recorded session. An inherited previous/named ID without authored-task acceptance is insufficient. When non-resumable, inspect possible effects and use **Replay from the node** for a deliberate attempt. Stop an unconfirmed native process first.                                                                                                                                                         |
| The provider refused the request (`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with `details.adapterCode: HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`; the message starts `The provider refused the request (HTTP 400, …)` and quotes the provider) | The provider refused a value the run's pinned definition sends, such as an effort or model it does not accept for this model or account. The failure keeps this cause even when the provenance says `delivery-uncertain` (Codex had already taken the prompt into its conversation). Resume is never offered, because the same request would be refused again. Correct the node, decision or default the message names, publish, and start a new run. |
| Session missing (`HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING`)                                                                                                                                                                  | Preserve and inspect the failed run. Resume is refused. Use **Replay from the node** for a deliberate attempt; named-session lookup can still select the same missing conversation. To change that policy, correct the definition and start a new run. For eligible failures use the explicit Start fresh session control described below (#265).                                                                                                     |

## Codex model unavailable for this account or endpoint

For a Codex inference turn, check the failed run's message, not just its top-level code. A structured provider refusal
(`HTTP 400`, `invalid_request_error`) appears as `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with
`details.adapterCode: HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`, followed by the provider's explanation.
When that explanation says the selected model is unavailable for the account or endpoint,
it identifies the cause of that request. A generic failure, malformed output, or an
unknown/transient error does not by itself establish an account restriction.

An enabled catalogue row and a successful **Retry preflight** do not test model access.
Preflight checks installation, CLI capabilities and login without sending a model turn.
Shipped model definitions and the bundled CLI's static plan information do not measure current
access; GraphGoblin's catalogue has no account-plan field. The `gpt-5.5` ChatGPT-account refusal reported in
[October 2026](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/427) is historical evidence,
not a current availability claim for your account. An API-key login is not a guaranteed remedy.

Choose a model the provider supports for the login and endpoint used by the API process, or
deliberately change that user's Codex login/provider configuration to a supported choice.
Correct the affected inference node or default, publish if the definition changed, and restart

A dispatch without a matching recorded outcome fails with resumable `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` (`outcome-uncertain`), including when writing progress or completion fails. A generic bookkeeping failure does not dispose the dispatch. Re-entering an unfinished script visit from an earlier build without a dispatch marker is also uncertain: missing provenance cannot prove the command never ran. Such visits never run automatically after upgrading. The previous attempt may already have produced its effect. In the inspector choose **Recover script**, then **Resume** to rerun knowingly, **Replay** to start a new run from that node, or **Cancel** to leave the run failed. Resume and Replay can repeat the effect; this is not an exactly-once guarantee (05).
 
+Commands use `shell: false`. Windows `.cmd` and `.bat` files therefore require an explicitly
+authored command processor; direct invocation is a proven `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`, not an
+automatic shell fallback. Ordinary Resume after that refusal keeps the pinned command and
+arguments. To change them, publish a corrected definition and start a new run. See
+[Windows batch commands](guide/07-troubleshooting.md#windows-batch-commands) for an example.
+
 Stdout and stderr use independent streaming UTF-8 decoders, so two-, three- and
 four-byte characters survive arbitrary subprocess chunk boundaries. Capture is
 limited to 10 MiB of raw bytes per stream by default (`ProcessScripts.maxOutputBytes`);

The same failure and recovery choices remain available if writing a dispatched script's progress or completion failed. Repair the storage fault, inspect any external effect, then choose Resume or Replay knowingly, or leave the run failed with Cancel. No store reset or migration is required.
 
+### Windows batch commands
+
+Script commands run without an implicit shell. On Windows, naming a `.cmd` or `.bat` file as
+the command fails with `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`: the process runner proved that it did not start.
+This is distinct from `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, which needs explicit recovery consent because
+an earlier attempt may have produced effects. A proven start refusal permits ordinary Resume,
+but Resume still uses the failed run's pinned command and arguments.

+To run a batch file, explicitly choose `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` (use your Windows
+installation's actual path), set its arguments to `/d`, `/c` and the intended batch command,
+and choose the working directory deliberately. `/d` disables the command processor's AutoRun
+commands. The command string after `/c` is interpreted by that shell; keep it authored and
+quote paths and arguments for `cmd.exe`, rather than inserting untrusted text. For example,
+with a working directory containing `build.cmd`, the arguments are `["/d", "/c", "build.cmd"]`.
+Publish the corrected definition and start a new run. Repeatedly resuming the old batch-file
+command cannot apply that definition change. If only an external prerequisite changed, such as
+restoring a missing executable, Resume can use the existing pinned definition.

content.content: 180	A run executes one immutable definition record for its whole life: the record its `versionId` names. Every executor start (the first, a wake after a wait, a resume, crash recovery) and every replay fork loads that record, never the loop's live draft. A published start pins the published version. A draft start (`allowDraft`, a test run) freezes the draft it read and validated into a `snapshot` record with its own id and the draft's number; the admission port commits the snapshot, the run, its initial thread and its `run.queued` event in one transaction. Editing, saving or publishing the draft afterwards never reaches the run. A snapshot cannot be started directly (`VERSION_NOT_PUBLISHED`), is not part of the version history, and storage triggers refuse its change, or its deletion while a run pins it.

# D197 bounded corrective review of F3: **ACCEPT FIX**

I found no introduced defect in the six changed paragraphs at `08633913a58cb42c32b4a18c72cd4aed67cfefa6`. Every changed statement matches the source I read, and the three documents agree with each other. This review used read-only file tools only; it is not QA and not merge permission. The sealed scan-3 `CHANGES_REQUIRED` record stands unchanged.

## Changed statements

All four #362-introduced publish instructions that F3 cited are corrected, plus the two generic run-guide passages. I confirmed the set of four against the two archived #362 patches (`docs/qa/2026-11-21-i4-362-batch-commands/author/candidate.patch` and `docs/qa/2026-11-21-i4-362-recovery-docs/freeze/source.patch`).

| Passage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/04-node-catalog.md:154-164` | Accurate. Carries fresh run, UI published version, API draft start, snapshot, trigger effect, Resume/Replay pin and external repair. |
| `docs/guide/03-run-and-observe.md:175` | Accurate. Same full set; publication is qualified to the UI path. |
| `docs/guide/03-run-and-observe.md:273` | Accurate. Short form, links to "Start through the API"; script consent text unchanged. |
| `docs/guide/03-run-and-observe.md:289` | Accurate. Short form with the same link. |
| `docs/guide/07-troubleshooting.md:150` | Accurate. Short form; `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` consent text unchanged. |
| `docs/guide/07-troubleshooting.md:210-224` | Accurate. The `cmd.exe` `/d` `/c` example, AutoRun explanation and untrusted-text caution are unchanged against the prior patch. |

The working-tree text of all six paragraphs matches the `+` lines of the root-freeze `source.patch`.

## Source trace

- **API draft start:** `apps/api/src/routes/runs.ts:72-129` accepts `versionId` and `allowDraft` and makes no publish or arm call. Line 96 falls back to `loop.currentVersionId`, so `allowDraft: true` alone never selects a draft. All six passages require both elements, which is correct.
- **Editable ID versus snapshot ID:** `packages/engine/src/run-manager.ts:3362-3385` refuses a snapshot ID with `VERSION_NOT_PUBLISHED` even with `allowDraft`, and refuses a draft without it. "Editable draft's `versionId`" is the right term in all six passages.
